# sigma_member_account_type (Resource)

Assigns an account type to an EXISTING Sigma member without owning the member's lifecycle. Use this when an external IdP (e.g. Okta) creates and deactivates users: this resource never creates a member and never deactivates one. Create fails if the member does not exist. Destroying the resource demotes the member back to `reset_to`. If the member is deactivated or removed out of band, the resource drops out of state instead of being recreated.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# For orgs where an IdP (e.g. Okta) creates and deactivates users. The member must
# already exist; destroying this resource demotes them to reset_to (default "Pro").
resource "sigma_member_account_type" "alice" {
  email        = "alice@example.com"
  account_type = "admin"
}

# Import by email.
# terraform import sigma_member_account_type.alice alice@example.com
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_type` (String) Account type name as Sigma stores it on the member (e.g. `admin`, `explorer`, `Pro`, or a custom account type name). Sigma normalizes some UI labels, so use the stored value (see `sigma_members`).
- `email` (String) Email of the existing member. Matched case-insensitively. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `reset_to` (String) Account type the member is moved to when this resource is destroyed. Defaults to `Pro`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Sigma member identifier (`memberId`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the member's email address.
terraform import sigma_member_account_type.example '<member_email>'
```
